title: Who was Gino Petralia?
article: The man who went on a murderous rampage in south Oshawa last weekend had a dark history of violence and brushes with the law.

Gino Petralia, 47, who was shot dead by police after a fatal attack on the Kelly family, had been charged in January with causing a disturbance in a public place and dangerous driving after an incident at the regional courthouse in Whitby.
A trial on those charges was to have begun Dec. 23 in Oshawa.
Before that, Mr. Petralia was charged three times with assault - twice in 2004 and once in 1998 - and also faced charges of impaired driving, failure to comply and failure to appear.

Durham Regional Police and the province's Special Investigations Unit (SIU) are investigating what led Mr. Petralia to fatally stab 26-year-old Leslie Kelly inside her family's townhouse at 1010 Glen St. Saturday evening, and viciously stab her husband Rick Kelly, 29, and their children, Nathan, 3, and Riley, 5.

It is believed the Kellys had recently gained custody of Mr. Petralia's son, Steven, 13, who is Rick's half-brother. Steven, Brandon and a 12-year-old cousin were in the house the night of the attack, but were not injured.
At his home in Oshawa yesterday, Mr. Petralia's uncle, Luigi, asked for privacy.
"We're trying to stay neutral," he said, visibly shaken. For about eight years, Mr. Petralia lived just two doors down with his mother, Luigi's sister.
Neighbours described the large family as warm and friendly, but said Mr. Petralia was always strange.
"Sometimes we'd see him shovelling the driveway, throwing the snow on the road," said one neighbour. "Then when he was done, he'd put it back. Stuff like that."
Mr. Petralia's mother did not answer the door Monday and when a floral delivery arrived in the afternoon, a neighbour offered to hold the flowers.
Members of the Petralia family said Tuesday they have been instructed by police not to speak to the media anymore.
